$comment: The canonical architecture that check-boundaries.mjs and check-layout.mjs apply when the app has no contracts/architecture.json, and the base its keys extend. {srcDir}, {servicesDir}, {dataDir}, {scriptsDir} and the other layout keys come from resolveLayout (rn-skills.config.json can move them). Keep the vendor and banned lists equal to the canonical eslint.config.mjs (VENDOR_SDK_PATHS, BANNED_PACKAGE_PATHS, ATT_ADAPTER, ADAPTERS; typescript-and-lint-rules owns it): change both together. The analytics SDKs beyond posthog-react-native are classified here only (an app that adopts one adds it to VENDOR_SDK_PATHS); the background task registry ({servicesDir}/*/define-*-tasks.ts, ESLint TASK_REGISTRIES) is an app contract entry (background-tasks lists it).
$compositionRoot: Files that may import adapters. Besides the three composition-root files and the root-kit registry (app-startup-and-bootstrap's src/services/create-root-kits.ts, which creates the optional kits' adapters from startApp), the data layer's device opener (persistence-and-migrations' src/data/open-device-database.ts) composes the SQL driver and the adapters that need the open database; the root layout calls it once. Its background twin (background-tasks' src/data/open-background-data.ts) does the same for each headless run, which never renders the root layout.
$frameworkPackages: What src/core may not import (core-pure): React and everything built on it. When node_modules exists, any package whose package.json lists react or react-native in dependencies or peerDependencies counts too.
$sdkPackagePatterns: Every package matching these names that bundled runtime code imports must be classified: in vendorSdks (a side effect behind a port) or in portlessSdks (UI building blocks and read-only facts). An unclassified one is the unclassified-sdk rule. The contract key sdkPackagePatterns adds names; when node_modules exists, a package that ships native code (expo-module.config.json, a *.podspec or android/build.gradle) counts too.

portlessSdks.expo-router: navigation: routes, layouts and the router hooks
portlessSdks.expo-splash-screen: holds and hides the splash screen during startup
portlessSdks.expo-application: reads the build's own facts (version, build number, application id)
portlessSdks.expo-asset: resolves and preloads bundled assets, like expo-font for fonts
portlessSdks.@expo/ui: renders SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose views
portlessSdks.expo-linking: builds and reads the app's own URLs (createURL, parse, useURL); openURL and openSettings leave the app, so a model hook calls them through a port, as it opens expo-web-browser
portlessSdks.expo-localization: reads the device locales once; language resolution takes them as values, so tests pass locales in

$gameFacing: What code of a game (src/games/<game>/ outside rules/ and levels/, which stay pure) may import besides its own folder. src/canvas is the shared canvas kit (skia-canvas-rendering, canvas-gestures-and-hit-testing) every game board draws and hit-tests with. The seam files game-session-host adds are recorded in the contract's gameFacing.

bannedPackages.axios: Network calls go through the ApiClient in src/api/ (fetch, typed and validated).
bannedPackages.@react-native-async-storage/async-storag: Use expo-sqlite/kv-store for preferences and expo-secure-store for secrets, behind a port.

$serverFiles: Expo Router server code: API routes (any +api file under the routes folder) and the one root +middleware file. They run on the server (EAS Hosting or another WinterCG host), and the native require.context leaves them out (expo-router 57.0.24, _ctx.ios.js and _ctx.android.js). The contract key serverFiles adds server helpers (src/server/**).
$serverPackages: Expo packages server code may import although their names look like runtime modules (expo-server 57.0.3, expo-router/server).
$nativeModulesDir: Where autolinking finds local Expo modules (npx create-expo-module --local): package.json expo.autolinking.nativeModulesDir, else ./modules (expo-modules-autolinking 57.0.13). Only an adapter imports one.
$testOnlyVariable: The variable whose comparison decides test-only code: a require() it decides belongs in a src/**/test-only.ts gate. The literal form and polarity of that comparison are app-variants-and-environment's inclusion-gate rule.
$assetExtensions: Metro's default assetExts plus Expo's additions (heic, avif, db), read from @expo/metro-config 57 (ExpoMetroConfig.js) on 2026-10-03, plus woff, woff2, lottie and riv, which apps add to assetExts. require() of a file with one of these extensions is how Metro bundles an asset.
